title: ANDS Studio — eCTD module builder
walkthrough:
You open a dossier and land on its module workspace, laid out in three columns.

The left column is the section tree. Its header shows an "M1"-style module badge, the module name, a progress bar, and an "X/Y required placed" count. A collapsed "Status key" button, marked with a help icon, reveals a tooltip legend of what each status means. Each section row carries a status icon with a hover tooltip, the section title and number, and a second line reading "Required" or "Optional," an optional lifecycle operator chip (NEW/REPL/APP/DEL, whose tooltip spells out whether it acts on a prior transmitted sequence), and the status word. Rows where AI drafting is available show a small sparkle icon. Two collapsible buckets at the bottom hold sections "Not in this submission model" and "Marked N/A by you."

The center column shows the selected section. An eyebrow reads "Module 1 · Section 1.2.2 · required," and, where the leaf sits, "Placed at … · leaf …." Below sit the title, a one-line purpose, and a "What Health Canada needs here" teach box with the guidance. Detail sits behind collapsed expanders: a "Format & source" (format, bilingual flag, and a "Health Canada guidance ↗" link), an "eCTD in plain language" primer (leaf, sequence, working vs active, the lifecycle operators, and a link to inspect the real backbone in the Application Viewer), and, on placed leaves, an "eCTD placement" expander. Expanded, that placement panel shows leaf id, node placement, href, sequence, the lifecycle operation with an explicit new/replace/append/delete note, a file fingerprint (md5, labelled as document control, not validation), and a "PDF/A — what this tool actually checks" box that lists the two checks it makes and states full PDF/A-1b conformance is not verified here — run eValidator before you transmit.

An action bar offers toggle buttons: "Upload," "Author in-app," and "Mark N/A." Upload shows a drop zone ("Drop a file or click to choose") with the accepted formats; bilingual sections show separate English and French zones. "Author in-app" opens a form; for AI-eligible sections a mode toggle appears first — "Draft with AI" or "Fill the form." A note explains the form produces a PDF/A leaf at the eCTD position, that known facts are pre-filled, and that fields tagged "example — replace this" show greyed example text you must replace; a warning names any fields still carrying the example. You click "Author [title] →" (or "Review vs Health Canada" first). A review panel reads "Health Canada review: no blocking content gaps." on pass, or "N to fix, M to check." with a bulleted list, each item carrying a suggested edit and an "HC guidance ↗" link.

The saved document card lists the filename, size, a "fingerprint md5" fragment, a provenance chip, and a "Download" link. While a draft holds example values or is an AI draft, a red banner reads "Not yet filable — review required."; a sample clears once no example values remain, while an AI draft needs the button "I have reviewed this AI draft — it is my content." Actions surface toast notifications.

The right column leads with a "Ready to transmit" card showing "● READY" or "● BLOCKED." If any sample or AI drafts are unconfirmed, a red banner names the count as "not yet filable." Three flags follow — "Documents," "Fee," and "Structural check" — each an icon plus label; the Structural-check tooltip states it is not Health Canada's official eValidator and to run eValidator before transmitting. A line notes how many items are still needed to file. Below sits a Draft completeness check, then one-line expanders for the "Submission tower (3D module view)," "Submission lifecycle & deficiency clock," "eCTD sequences & package export" (which force-opens and shows "export blocked" when blocked), a Module 1 "Bilingual / XML Product Monograph detail," and "Collaboration & task assignments." Selecting another section swaps the center panel; completing work updates the progress bar and the row's status icon.
